Article Title: 'Won't move forward without public': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu amid protests over Siang mega dam
Article Text:
Siang mega dam: Khandu seeks cooperation for report, says project won't be imposed

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu has assured residents that the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) will not be imposed on them, saying the government is currently seeking cooperation only to complete its Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR).Speaking to reporters, Khandu said he was inviting the youth wing of Adi Bane Kebang (ABK) and the Adi Students' Union (AdiSU) for discussions following their recent media briefings on the project."I want to reach out to all the associations and units in the Siang area to try and provide more clarity about this project. Right now, we aren't even talking about building the dam. Right now, only the PFR needs to happen," he said.Khandu said a decision on whether to proceed with the dam would be taken only after the PFR establishes its feasibility. Even if the project is found viable, the government would consult residents in accordance with legal provisions, he added."This project won't move forward without talking to the public," Khandu said, adding that he was encouraged by the response from local organisations during his recent interactions.He said he would continue visiting the Siang region until the PFR process was completed.The chief minister also alleged that residents, particularly in Siang and Upper Siang districts, were being fed misinformation about the project. He said the government wanted to address their concerns through direct engagement.The proposed 11,200-megawatt project is planned on the Siang river and is being pursued by the Centre through NHPC. Envisaged as a multipurpose storage project, it is expected to combine hydropower generation with water management and strategic objectives.However, sections of the indigenous Adi community have consistently opposed the project, citing concerns over the possible submergence of villages, displacement, loss of ancestral land and livelihoods, and environmental damage. The project's location in a seismically active region has also raised questions about dam safety.Protests intensified in October, with demonstrations turning violent in late September and again on October 23. Protesters set fire to an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, while several vehicles and properties linked to political leaders were damaged.The unrest has prompted additional security deployment and renewed efforts by the state government to initiate dialogue. The Arunachal Indigenous Tribes Forum has also proposed setting up a peace committee to facilitate discussions between the government and groups opposing the project.Khandu's latest outreach comes amid continuing demands from local organisations for meaningful consultations and a halt to survey activities until their concerns are addressed.Tensions have persisted over the past week. On October 25, Khandu held separate meetings with legislators and indigenous community representatives to discuss the PFR, environmental concerns and national security implications. On October 29, a solidarity rally in Itanagar demanded the release of detained protesters and the withdrawal of cases.The Arunachal Indigenous Tribes Forum has since proposed a peace committee to facilitate dialogue.India's biggest proposed hydropower project, spread across three districts of Arunachal Pradesh's Siang valley, is being positioned as a strategic counter to China's mega dam planned upstream.However, the project has faced resistance from indigenous communities, particularly members of the Adi tribe, who fear that the reservoir could submerge villages and disrupt their deep-rooted ties with the Siang river.
Article Summary: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu has assured residents that the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project will not be imposed on them. He said the government is currently seeking cooperation only to complete its Pre- Feasibility Report (PFR) The proposed 11,200-megawatt project is planned on the Siang river and is being pursued by the Centre.

NEW DELHI: A helicopter with six people onboard crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district while travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun. One pilot and five passengers were on board the chopper. The wreckage of a helicopter has been found.The helicopter, reportedly operated by Charlie X-ray Company, was reported missing near Hathi Parvat, prompting authorities to deploy two other choppers to locate it.Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel have been dispatched to the site for relief and rescue operations, officials told PTI."At 14.21hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, disaster management department, and SDRF,” Dhami wrote in a post on X.He added that he was personally monitoring the situation and that instructions had been issued to airlift the seriously injured to advanced medical facilities for treatment.

Article Title: 'Swimming competition?' Kiren Rijiju's playful challenge as Manoj Tiwari invites Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal for Yamuna dip
Article Text:
After Tiwari's Yamuna dip, Rijiju floats idea of swimming contest

NEW DELHI: After BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna and praised the river's "cleanliness", his party colleague and Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday proposed a "swimming competition" between the two.Sharing Tiwari's video on X, Rijiju wrote: "Manoj ji, don't you think that in Yamuna ji's much cleaner water, there could be a swimming competition between the two of us?"Ahead of Chhath Puja , Tiwari on Thursday took a dip and swam in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar in Delhi. The North East Delhi MP praised the efforts to clean the river under the leadership of chief minister Rekha Gupta.Tiwari said he was “overjoyed” that the work had made it possible for him to enter the river. He credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Gupta, saying the aim was to provide Delhi residents with a clean Yamuna.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here? I will tell Arvind Kejriwal that this is all a sign of cleanliness. There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water,” Tiwari said.He added that his visit was meant to send a message and was not intended to shame Kejriwal.The Aam Aadmi Party, however, disputed Tiwari's claims, saying its workers had visited the site and exposed what it called the BJP's false claims about the river's cleanliness.A party worker claimed that the water at the site was black and heavily polluted. The workers also said Tiwari had taken a dip during a Yamuna ghat cleaning drive and described his claim of drinking the river water as “completely false”.AAP accused Tiwari, who is from Purvanchal, of “staging theatrics” ahead of Chhath Puja. It also issued an open challenge to the BJP MP, saying, “Take a dip where the drain water flows into the Yamuna, drink the water and livestream the entire exercise for the public across all your social media accounts. People elected Manoj Tiwari as their MP because they trusted him, but he is trying to mislead the people of Delhi.”
Article Summary: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna and praised the river's "cleanliness" Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday proposed a "swimming competition" between the two. Aam Aadmi Party, however, said its workers had visited the site and exposed what it called the BJP's false claims.

Article Title: ‘Class 12-pass mafia’: Bengal LoP Ritabrata Banerjee hits back at Abhishek's warning to cops
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Bengal assembly Ritabrata Banerjee on Friday hit back at Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee over his warning to police officers in West Bengal. He called him arrogant and urged the state government to register a suo motu case over his remarks.He also challenged Abhishek to walk alone to the Kali Mata temple without security, questioning his claim that he enjoyed the protection of the people."The lower the level of education, the higher the level of arrogance. This individual has only passed Class 12—he is a "Class 12-pass" member of this "chartered mafia." That is why his arrogance is so extreme," Ritabrata said.He accused Abhishek of threatening police personnel and officers despite the people having voted for a change of government. "The people have changed the government; the public gave their mandate against us. Yet, there is no shortage of arrogance. The way he was speaking—he was threatening police personnel and officers," he said.Ritabrata also questioned Abhishek's decision to seek security after previously claiming that he did not need it. Referring to an alleged incident in which Abhishek was beaten for being a thief, he said the TMC leader had earlier maintained that he had the "security of the people"."Diamond Harbour is quite far away, but let him try stepping out of his home alone and walking to the Kali Mata temple. He should at least try doing that," Ritabrata said.He further claimed that Abhishek had approached the court seeking full-fledged security, despite previously saying that he needed no protection."I urge the state government to register a suo motu case and take cognisance of the matter. The state government must take action," he added.The remarks came a day after Abhishek warned police officers allegedly targeting TMC workers that they would face consequences if his party returned to power. He said he was maintaining a list of officers who were acting at the behest of West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari."I am keeping a list of names. None will be spared once the government changes," Abhishek had said.He accused police officers of implicating thousands of TMC workers in false cases to secure favourable postings. He also alleged that an IPS officer in Paschim Medinipur had targeted party workers despite earlier congratulating him on the TMC's expected electoral victory.The exchange comes amid a political confrontation between the BJP and the TMC following the arrest of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen over alleged financial irregularities linked to Durga Puja preview shows and the sale of passes.Suvendu has alleged that Sen may not have been the only beneficiary of the suspected irregularities, suggesting that the investigation could reach senior political figures, including former chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He has maintained that the law would take its course irrespective of the influence of those under investigation.
Article Summary: Leader of opposition in Bengal assembly Ritabrata Banerjee hits back at TMC leader. Accuses Abhishek of threatening police personnel and officers despite people having voted for a change of government. He also challenged Abhis hek to walk alone to the Kali Mata temple without security.

NEW DELHI: The six people on board a helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation died after it crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday afternoon. The helicopter was travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun when it crashed into a hillside near Chai village."All six people on board chopper that crashed in Joshimath have died, their bodies found," Chamoli Superintendent of Police Surjit Singh Panwar told PTI.The helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm. Authorities lost track of it while it was crossing the Joshimath Valley and it was subsequently reported missing near Hathi Parvat.Search and rescue teams, including personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Army, police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), were deployed to the area following reports of the crash.According to the available details, six people were on board the helicopter, including the pilot and five passengers, all reportedly from Bengaluru. Their identities are as follows:Captain HimanshuSpeaking to PTI in Dehradun, Prateek Jain, CEO of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), said "the helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm today.As it was crossing the Joshimath Valley, we suddenly lost track of it on our tracking system, which we use to monitor its movements. We have also received some local information regarding the incident.""So far, nothing has been confirmed. However, according to the information available in the passenger manifest, a total of six people were on board the helicopter, the pilot and five passengers. The helicopter's location has not yet been traced. However, search and rescue teams have been mobilised in coordination with the Chamoli district administration," he said."The SDRF has also been deployed, along with a unit of the Army. As soon as the weather clears, we will send another rescue helicopter from here to locate the missing helicopter," Jain added.Local inputs about the incident also prompted authorities to initiate a search operation.Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal of Joshimath police post said information about the incident was received from the Joshimath sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) at 2.21 pm."At 14:21 hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area," Kanyal told ANI."In this regard, UCADA officials stated that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter, which was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara, is showing near the Army Camp above Chai village. Complete details regarding the crash or crash landing are not yet available," he added.Speaking to ANI, Jain said the helicopter belonged to Trans Bharat Aviation and confirmed that the company’s entire fleet had been grounded as a precautionary measure."A helicopter belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation departed from Badrinath for the Sahastradhara heliport at 1:14 PM. We have been unable to trace the helicopter's location since it was passing through the vicinity of the Joshimath valley. Upon receiving this information, we mobilised the Chamoli district administration, the SDRF (State Disaster Response Force), and an Army unit to the area near the incident site to prepare for a proper rescue operation," he said."As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of helicopters belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation has been grounded...According to initial information, there were 6 people on board—the pilot plus 5 others. We will share further details once we have confirmation..." he added.The grounding is a precautionary step as authorities work to establish the circumstances surrounding the crash.Uttarakhand disaster management officials in Chamoli district said teams had rushed to the area to conduct search and rescue operations. Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel were dispatched to the reported crash site.The location of the helicopter and the condition of the people on board remained unclear in the initial hours after the incident. Authorities were coordinating with the district administration and other agencies to locate the aircraft and assess the situation.It was also not immediately confirmed whether the helicopter was returning after ferrying pilgrims from the Badrinath shrine.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said he was closely monitoring the situation and that a joint rescue operation was under way.In a post on X, Dhami said, "Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF.""I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers," Dhami added.The state government said the rescue operation was being coordinated by the district administration and disaster management authorities.The crash took place amid adverse weather conditions in Uttarakhand, with rainfall and snowfall reported in several parts of the state.Television channels reported that fire and smoke were visible at the crash site and that rescue teams had reached the area. Bad weather was suspected to have contributed to the incident, though the cause had not been officially established.Kedarnath Dham witnessed the season's first heavy snowfall following continuous snowfall since Thursday, October 29. The surrounding hills were covered in snow, while temperatures in the region dropped significantly.The India Meteorological Department's Dehradun centre also forecast continued rainfall over the next few days, particularly in the hill districts.Dr CS Tomar, director of the Meteorological Centre in Dehradun, said heavy rainfall had been recorded at eight to nine places across Uttarakhand on October 29, particularly in Uttarkashi, Tehri and Haridwar districts.Tomar said similar weather conditions were expected on Friday, with a higher likelihood of rainfall in the Kumaon region."Tomorrow, on the 31st, chances of light to very light rain will persist, especially in the hilly districts. Similarly, on the 1st and 2nd (of November), light to very light rain may be witnessed at isolated places, particularly in our northern hilly districts," he said.In view of the forecast, district administrations have been placed on alert to ensure the safety of pilgrims, residents and commuters.Earlier on Thursday, District Magistrate Prashant Arya directed officials to activate the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) in alert mode to monitor weather conditions and oversee precautionary measures.Authorities are also monitoring road conditions and the Gangotri and Yamunotri shrines through live CCTV cameras.The administration has appealed to devotees and pilgrims to take precautions against the cold and follow advisories issued by the administration and police.
Article Summary: The helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm today. Authorities lost track of it while it was crossing the Joshimath Valley and it was subsequently reported missing near Hathi Parvat. Search and rescue teams, including personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Army, police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), were deployed to the area following reports of the crash.

Karnataka Congress sacks Kripa Alva

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) on Saturday expelled former party general secretary Kripa Alva for six years over her alleged involvement in a sting operation targeting Congress leaders in the state. The expulsion takes immediate effect, according to an order issued by KPCC vice-president M Narayanaswamy.The order said the controversy had caused embarrassment to the party because of negative publicity and media reactions. It also cited alleged anti-party activities as the reason for the disciplinary action."As your name has figured in this sting operation case and your conduct in the matter amounts to anti-party activities, on the instructions of the Hon'ble KPCC President, you are hereby expelled from the party for a period of six years with immediate effect," the order stated.According to the KPCC, a show-cause notice had previously been issued to Alva seeking her explanation over the allegations. However, the party said she had not submitted any response so far.The action comes amid an ongoing police investigation into a video allegedly targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah.Siddaramaiah had named her behind the 'defamatory video'. The Bengaluru police said on Thursday that the sexual abuse allegation featured in the video was part of a "fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative"."The evidence gathered so far prima facie indicates that the allegations of sexual abuse portrayed in the video are part of a fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative," the police said in a statement.The police further said that statements recorded from individuals appearing in the video and the evidence collected so far did not substantiate the allegations."Their statements and the evidence collected so far, prima facie, with regard to the allegations made or implied in the recording about any individuals mentioned in the video, is false and concocted," the statement said.Investigators said the original mobile phone allegedly used to record the video had been traced, recovered and seized. It has been sent for forensic examination, with the report awaited.According to the police, the video was allegedly recorded in 2023 and purportedly concerned an incident dating back to 2011. Investigators are examining whether the recording was staged, fabricated or manipulated and are tracing its circulation before it appeared on social media in September-October 2026.The police also said the video was uploaded through anonymous accounts using VPNs, masked IP addresses and spoofed phone numbers. A mobile phone allegedly linked to the YouTube upload was traced to a shop dealing in used and refurbished devices in Delhi.One person connected with the procurement of the device was arrested from the National Capital Region on October 24. Police said preliminary findings suggested that he worked as a freelance social media content creator and may have links with politically connected individuals in New Delhi. These associations are being investigated.Alva had earlier appeared before the Central Crime Branch (CCB) on October 26, where she was questioned and her statement recorded. Police sources quoted by news agency ANI said she had also been questioned on previous occasions.Siddaramaiah had named Alva in connection with the alleged sting operation and obtained a court injunction restraining media organisations from airing or publishing the video. His son and minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah had also alleged the involvement of some Congress leaders.The investigation remains ongoing, with police examining the video's creation, ownership, circulation and the identities and possible motives of those involved.
Article Summary: Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) on Saturday expelled former party general secretary Kripa Alva. The expulsion takes immediate effect, according to an order issued by KPCC vice-president M Narayanaswamy. The order said the controversy had caused embarrassment to the party.

Article Title: Omar Abdullah faces internal storm: Many NC MLAs upset over J&K cabinet rejig; Srinagar MP announces resignation
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah and Farukh Abdullah (File photo)

MLAs meeting

SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of legislators reportedly unhappy over the recent cabinet expansion and seeking greater democracy within the party and resignation of the whole cabinet.The discontent within the party has taken place at a time when the party MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. “I will resign from the National Conference and my Lok Sabha seat on November 3, 2026. The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family. They expect the people to vote, then know their place. They take us for fools who cannot tell a broken promise from a political necessity. Ask them to honour their own manifesto, and they lecture us on how little we understand realpolitik,” Mehdi wrote on X.“We demanded the restoration of Article 370, the release of prisoners and the protection of our rights. They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver. We refuse to lend our name to this humiliation. There is no fixing this rot from within. The seat was won on a promise to the people,” Mehdi added.Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise.Mehdi would address the people on November 3, the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam. His father was a Congress leader and prominent Shiite cleric who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.Ruhullah Mehdi is an alumnus of Tyndale Biscoe School and holds a bachelor's degree in arts from the University of Kashmir. His political career began in 2002, when he contested and won his first Assembly election from Budgam. He retained the seat in 2008 and 2014. In 2009, he was inducted into the state Cabinet, becoming the youngest Cabinet minister. In 2015, Mehdi was nominated as the chief Spokesperson of the National Conference, the position he held for several years. However, after abrogation of Article 370 on August 5, 2019, he distanced himself from the party’s stand of maintaining silence over the situation in Jammu and Kashmir after August 5. He would urge the party to take a stand on Article 370 rather than urging the centre to restore statehood which he describes as a scaled down position.In August this year the NC president Dr Abdullah said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary elections without the NC support. He said that if Mehdi believed Article 370 could be restored, he should fight for it, as no one had stopped him from pursuing the cause. Dr Abdullah had said the NC had not prevented Mehdi from pushing for the restoration of Article 370. Dr Abdullah had said Mehdi should resign and contest elections on his own. In response Mehdi had said that Dr Abdullah has for the first time asked anything from him and he will not disappoint him.Meanwhile, according to the sources, over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of the chief minister’s advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani.In a related development, NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah removed Mubarak Gul as the party’s general secretary. Gul was among the MLAs who attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. After the cabinet expansion on Tuesday, Dr Abdullah had elevated Gul, who wanted cabinet induction for himself, to the post of general secretary.Omar Abdullah and Dr. Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi.Dismissing reports of widespread discontent within the party and rebellion, NC spokesperson Ifra Jan questioned the claim that 20 MLAs attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. “They are saying 20 MLAs held this particular meeting. Where is this figure of 20 coming from? Is there a photograph or a list of names? Somebody anonymously claims 20 and everyone else repeats it without any investigative corroboration,” she said.“After the cabinet expansion, I think one or two MLAs openly expressed their displeasure and that was there for everyone to see. Isn’t that normal? Doesn’t this happen in all political parties? Some MLAs are happy while others are unhappy. This is common practice across the country,” she said.“Ever since Omar Sahib (Omar Abdullah) took oath, the leader of the opposition BJP's Sunil Sharma, has been claiming that the government will fall next week. Unfortunately, nobody is asking why. Every disagreement is being viewed through the prism of “government will fall rumours” without any evidence. We consider any claim of large-scale discontent within the party as a rumour,” she added. Sunil Sharma said it seems Omar Abdullah government has only eight MLAs with it and those eight are cabinet Ministers.Nazir Gurezi, who was part of the meeting, told the TOI that Lone had invited all MLAs and “large number of MLAs were at his residence. We just had food there”.On Tuesday morning Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly inducted ministers, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo at Lok Bhawan in Srinagar taking the number to eight with Omar including nine. Omar dropped Satish Sharma, who was Minister for food, consumer affairs, transport science, IT, youth affairs, sports, and training.Omar was sworn in as chief minister on October 16, 2024, along with five ministers. Under the prescribed norms, the council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly. With 90 members, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly can have a maximum of nine ministers, including the chief minister. Three cabinet berths had remained vacant for nearly two years as the party struggled to decide whom to induct.Soon after the expansion on Tuesday, NC MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi broke down. “I deserved a place in the cabinet. I felt very sad not to be part of the cabinet. I was deserving of it (cabinet seat). Till the last moment, I was expecting to be part of the cabinet,” Larmi said. “I am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,” he had said.Mubarak Gul’s supporters lodged a protest at the party headquarters.In the 90-member Assembly, the NC has 41 MLAs and is backed by six independent legislators, while the Congress, with six MLAs, extends support to the government from outside.
Article Summary: Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise. Over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers.

Article Title: Bhutan GLOF creates new lake downstream, raises fears of secondary hazards
Article Text:
Bengal spared Bhutan GLOF impact, water of Sankosh recedes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

DEHRADUN/KOLKATA/GUWAHATI: A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) originating in Bhutan, which prompted an alert across parts of Assam and West Bengal on Friday, has led to the formation of a new temporary lake downstream, raising concerns about a possible secondary hazard.Bhutan’s National Centre for Hydrology and Meteorology (NCHM) confirmed that the outburst had led to the creation of a new artificial lake at Taktsemakhang, situated at the confluence of Sintaphu Chhu and Lungu Chhu, also known as Gangchen Tag Chhu. The newly formed body of water is being monitored for any potential secondary flood hazard, with NCHM advising residents in the Mochhu and Punatsangchhu river valleys to remain vigilant and avoid riverbanks and low-lying areas.The Oct 29 GLOF originated from Shintaphu glacial lake which, according to International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) estimates, contained 6 to 7 million cubic metres of water, equivalent to approximately 2,400-2,800 Olympic-size swimming pools, before the breach. The volume of water released remains under assessment. India’s Central Water Commission (CWC) subsequently issued a special flood advisory for West Bengal and Assam, warning that water levels in Alipurduar and Dhubri districts could rise sharply as floodwaters moved downstream through the Sankosh river system.West Bengal had issued a high alert across north Bengal but the GLOF has had little or no impact in the state. On Friday morning, as water from the Bhutan hills came downstream, the Sankosh river rose 1.5 metres from its normal level but began receding soon. By Friday afternoon it appeared the crisis was over and people who had taken refuge in flood centres returned to their homes. No damage was reported. The Alipurduar district administration had opened 18 flood shelters in Kumargramduar block on Thursday night and around 10,000 people living along the banks of the Sankosh in Kumargram tea estate, Kumargram forest village, Pakriguri and Bholka had taken refuge in these shelters along with a couple of thousand from Assam.Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the state was closely monitoring the possible impact of the glacial lake outburst across all vulnerable revenue circles of Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts. “Our teams … are ready to respond if needed. Residents are requested to stay alert, follow official updates and cooperate with officials,” he said.According to Bhutan’s national daily “Kuensel”, the GLOF sent floodwaters down the Mochhu river, damaging roads, bridges and public infrastructure in Gasa and Punakha. No casualties have been reported. Floodwaters washed away facilities at Gasa Tshachu, damaged sections of the Punakha-Gasa Secondary National Highway and the Gasa-Laya road, and swept away a Bailey bridge in Punakha built in 2022 with Indian support.Ashim Sattar, a glacial hazard expert at IIT Bhubaneswar, told TOI that the formation of temporary lakes downstream is a known risk during such disasters. “During GLOFs, powerful floodwaters erode river valleys and carry large amounts of debris, which can temporarily block river channels and form new lakes. Such lakes generally drain naturally, but they can also become secondary flood hazards if not regularly monitored,” Sattar said.He explained that Shintaphu was a medium-sized glacial lake located close to the Lunana glacial lake complex, a cluster of four lakes, including Thorthormi, considered one of Bhutan’s most hazardous.According to NCHM, the flood crossed Taktsemakhang around 8.27 pm on Thursday. Warning sirens along Mochhu and downstream Punatsangchhu were activated as monitoring stations recorded a sharp rise in river levels. At Yebesa, the water level peaked at 6.7 m at 11 pm before receding to a normal level of 2.84 m around 12.30 am on Friday, a drop of 3.86 m within 90 minutes.Sattar noted that timely activation of the regional early-warning network prevented loss of life.The incident highlights the growing threat of cascading disasters in the Himalayas, where an initial glacial breach can trigger secondary hazards downstream through valley erosion, sediment deposition and temporary river blockages.Previous assessments by ICIMOD and UNDP identified 47 major potentially dangerous glacial lakes (PDGLs) across the transboundary Koshi, Gandaki and Karnali river basins. Current estimates show that 388 GLOFs have been documented across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region, including Karakoram and the central and eastern Himalayas.In 2015, a GLOF in the headwaters of the Mo Chuu river, where Sintaphu lake is located, prompted Bhutanese authorities to work with the SERVIR-Himalaya initiative to assess glacial lake risks in the catchment, according to experts at ICIMOD.
Article Summary: Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) originating in Bhutan has led to the formation of a new temporary lake downstream. The newly formed body of water is being monitored for any potential secondary flood hazard. West Bengal had issued a high alert across north Bengal but the GLOF has had little or no impact.

Article Title: J&K cops bust terror financing syndicate, 10 held
Article Text:
J&K Police bust terror financing module in Shopian

SRINAGAR: J&K Police Friday said they have busted a terror financing module and arrested 10 suspects from different parts of the union territory.“During the investigation, suspicious online financial transactions carried out through various payment platforms were analysed, leading to the tracing of money trails across multiple layers. The investigation revealed a wider network of individuals allegedly involved in terror financing and having links with terrorists and their associates lodged in different jails,” the police said in a statement here.“So far, 10 terrorist associates have been arrested and an FIR registered at police station in Shopian,” police said.“Initial Investigation revealed the accused were clandestinely collecting and raising funds from the general public and channelising the money through established financial links to facilitate the terrorist activities of LeT/The Resistance Front (TRF). The funds were also allegedly being utilised to provide logistical support, including smartphones, for furthering terrorist activities,” the police said, adding that further investigation is underway.

The funds were also allegedly being utilised to provide logistical support.

Article Title: HC seeks status report on reuniting deported Pak-born teen with Indian father in J&K
Article Text:
J&K HC asks Rajouri admin to report on Pakistan-born teen's return to Indian father

SRINAGAR: J&K and Ladakh high court sought a compliance report Friday from the Rajouri district administration on its March 25 order to reunite a Pakistan-born teenager deported after the Pahalgam terror attack with his Indian father on grounds of “sacrosanct human values and rights”.Justice MA Chowdhary’s seven-month-old order, iterated by the single-judge bench of Justice Rahul Bharti, equated the boy’s plight with the “human suffering” and estrangement caused by Partition. “The instant case stems out of this tragedy,” the court said, rejecting the Bureau of Immigration’s contention that the boy had been deported because he didn’t have an active visa.Aasim Sajjad, aka Fardin Sajjad, was born to Rajouri-based govt schoolteacher Sajjad Ahmed and a Pakistani woman, Shabnum Kouser of Rawali in Gujranwala. The marriage took place in Pakistan in Dec 2005 and Aasim was born there on Nov 26 the next year.Sajjad’s wife and son visited India in Oct 2007 on a 90-day visa, which was later extended on marital grounds until 2013. When his wife died on June 5, 2013, Ahmed sought an extension of his son’s visa, granted until April 20, 2015. He then purportedly filed repeated applications for Indian citizenship or visa extension on compassionate grounds, none of which was taken up.Ahmed alleged that J&K Police raided his house on April 29, 2025, took his son away in a van and deported him through the Wagah border without informing him or handing over a deportation order. The deportation came after the Union govt cancelled visas to all Pakistani citizens after the April 22 terrorist attack on tourists in Pahalgam and ordered them to leave.In its objections, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) argued that Ahmed didn’t “come to court with clean hands” and that his son had been staying in India without a valid visa and was legally bound to leave. The FRRO counsel said the status of the teenager’s citizenship application, which Ahmed claims to have filed, remains “not received yet” on the MHA portal.
Article Summary: J&K HC asks Rajouri admin to report on Pakistan-born teen's return to Indian father. Justice MA Chowdhary's seven-month-old order equated the boy’s plight with the ‘human suffering’ and estrangement caused by Partition.

SRINAGAR: J&K health minister Sakina Itoo, in a letter to lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha , flagged the practice of closing off both ends of Srinagar-Anantnag-Kulgam-Qazigund national highway for civilian traffic during the movement of Army vehicles, stating that it was distressing to see ambulances stranded, students missing classes, and ordinary citizens waiting 15-30 minutes, sometimes even hours, for convoy movement.“What fault have our people committed to endure such hardships?” Itoo asked, urging the LG, who is in charge of law and order and security in the Union Territory, to “explore practical traffic management measures that uphold essential security protocols while ensuring uninterrupted passage for ambulances and minimising public inconvenience”.Following the Pulwama terror strike, Centre had issued directions restricting civilian traffic “for some time” to let security forces’ convoys pass on the highway. NEW DELHI: Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh has accused sections of the state BJP leadership of conspiring with the Congress to remove him from office. Singh also questioned the continued violence in the state since his resignation in February 2025.In an exclusive interview with PTI, Singh said the BJP government must urgently work to "regain the lost confidence and trust of the people" ahead of assembly elections due early next year. He also claimed there was strong public demand for his return as chief minister."I had not been treated well since 2017. I am not accusing the Delhi leadership but sections of the state leaders who conspired against me with the Congress,” Singh told PTI. He alleged that some party colleagues resented his elevation despite having switched from the Congress to the BJP.“There are MLAs who could never accept how I became CM twice after having crossed over from the Congress. They consider BJP as their property. So they plotted, planned and made me resign," he added.Singh also challenged the argument that his removal would help restore peace in the state, pointing to continuing clashes involving Meitei, Kuki and Naga communities.The present government, led by Y Khemchand Singh, took office in February this year."Now Biren is out. So, what happened now? How many Naga brothers have died? They were blaming me. They were saying I favour the majority. Now it is Christians versus Christians. Where has the European Union gone?" he asked.His remarks come amid renewed violence in the state. Three Meitei villagers were shot dead and three others injured in an ambush by suspected militants inside a forest along the Imphal East-Kangpokpi border on Monday. The victims were part of a group collecting firewood near Nongshum and Khongbal Tangkhul villages when the attack took place.The killings triggered protests in Imphal, with demonstrators carrying the bodies of two victims to a sit-in outside the chief minister's official residence. Security personnel later used tear gas to disperse the crowd. The latest killings come amid escalating clashes between Kuki-Zo and Naga groups in the hill districts, with more than 50 people reportedly killed on either side over the past eight months.Expressing concern over the BJP's declining public confidence, Singh also questioned the government's commitment to issues that had featured prominently during his tenure, including the anti-drug campaign and action against illegal immigration."That is my main worry," he told PTI when asked whether public anxiety could hurt the BJP in the elections."Anti-drug campaign, anti-poppy plantation, that campaign we are not seeing. The government should also continue biometric identification of suspected illegal immigrants. At least identify them. And even if you can't deport the illegal immigrants at least you can keep them in camps. What we have started, continue it. And save the future. We have to save the future," he said.
Article Summary: Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh has accused sections of the state BJP leadership of conspiring with the Congress to remove him from office. Singh also questioned the continued violence in the state since his resignation in February 2025. He said the BJP government must urgently work to "regain the lost confidence and trust of the people"

Article Title: 'I will be present in court': Anant Singh to surrender by Dec 1 after SC cancels bail; accuses Neeraj Kumar of plotting case
Article Text:
Anant SIngh

Anant Singh recounts events leading to murder

Singh links expulsion to dispute with Neeraj Kumar

NEW DELHI: Expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Friday said he would surrender before the court by December 1 in compliance with the Supreme Court 's order cancelling his bail in the Dularchand Yadav murder case.He accused newly elected JD(U) MLC Neeraj Kumar of orchestrating the case against him and claimed that he had been deliberately implicated.Reacting to the Supreme Court's decision, Singh said he had faith in the judiciary and would abide by its directions. He also expressed confidence that he would be granted bail again."We will surrender. The court is not our enemy; whatever the court has decided is acceptable to us. The court will grant us bail again later. We have faith in the judiciary. We always had faith, and we still have faith today," Singh told reporters in Patna.Asked when he would surrender, the Mokama MLA said, "Why should I surrender early? I have full faith in the court and the judiciary. On whatever date is designated for me, I will be present in court."He subsequently confirmed that he would appear before the court on December 1.Singh alleged that Neeraj Kumar was behind the legal action against him and had ensured that his name was included in the murder case."This incident was orchestrated by Neeraj Kumar. First, from 3 kilometres away, he got my name added to the Dularchand murder case. After that, when I had been on bail here for six months, Neeraj took the case to Delhi. We only found out after everything had already transpired. They never issued any notice or informed us of anything; they did everything behind the scenes," he alleged.Asked whether he believed the Supreme Court's decision was the result of Neeraj Kumar's opposition, Singh said, "No, we don't believe that. You people claim the government did it--we don't accept that. Neeraj did it."He also accused Neeraj Kumar of being behind Yadav's murder and claimed that false witnesses had been brought forward to implicate him.“Neeraj got Dularchand murdered himself. He orchestrated it to immediately implicate Anant Singh and send him to jail. He brought false witnesses from his own locality, made them testify,” Singh alleged.Recounting the events of October 30, 2025, Singh claimed that he was campaigning for votes when his convoy crossed paths with a vehicle carrying Dularchand Yadav, who was supporting a Jan Suraaj Party candidate."During the election, we were out asking for votes. There was a Jan Suraaj candidate, and Dularchand was in that vehicle. As we were returning after campaigning, we crossed paths with Dularchand on the road. After that, he went his way, and we went ours. When we had travelled about 4 to 5 kilometres, news spread that a clash had erupted right where we had just eaten," he said.Singh maintained that he learnt about Yadav's murder only after returning from campaigning in another village.According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran him over with an SUV. Singh has denied the allegations and previously claimed that Jan Suraaj supporters attacked his convoy first.The expelled MLA also linked his removal from the JD(U) to his differences with Neeraj Kumar, saying the party leadership had acted in support of the MLC."The party claims we opposed the party--we did not oppose the party, we opposed Neeraj," he said, referring to his campaign for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh against the JD(U)'s official nominee Neeraj Kumar in the Patna Graduates' constituency MLC election.Singh expressed confidence in former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, claiming that the developments would not have taken place had the JD(U) leader been in good health and actively involved in party affairs."I firmly believe that had Nitish Kumar ji been in good health and conscious of things, this would never have happened. The party wouldn’t have tossed me out like a fly from milk. Now that they have expelled me, the party will reap what it sows. They will struggle even to open their account," Singh said.Asked if he considered the matter a case of political vendetta, he said, “No, it isn’t politics. It is personal. It’s Neeraj. And the party backed Neeraj.”Singh said he would not approach any political leader for intervention and would follow the court's directions."I will not go to anyone regarding this matter. Nowhere at all. Whatever the court directs, I will abide by the court's word. If the court summons me, I will go to court," he said.On the multiple cases registered against him, Singh said, “Deceitful people keep implicating me, and I keep getting justice from the courts. By count, there may be 60 or 70 cases. When the judges examine the facts, they will deliver justice to me. I have done nothing wrong.”Earlier on Friday, the Supreme Court cancelled the bail granted to Singh by the Patna High Court on March 19, 2026, and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the High Court had erred in granting bail without adequately considering the gravity of the offence and Singh's criminal antecedents. The bail order was challenged by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of the deceased.The development comes days after the JD(U) expelled Singh and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years, citing anti-party activities. Following the action, the Bihar government removed Neelam Devi from her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee and withdrew her Minister of State rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.The party has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the Anti-Defection Law.
Article Summary: Expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Kumar Singh says he will surrender before the court by December 1 in compliance with the Supreme Court's order cancelling his bail in the Dularchand Yadav murder case. Singh claims he was deliberately implicated in the case and accused newly elected MLC Neeraj Kumar of orchestrating it.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK.
