Article Title: German, Slovak nationals die in 5-star Bengaluru hotel pool; US guest, pool attendant injured while trying to rescue them
Article Text:
On Friday evening, two foreign nationals from Germany and Slovakia died from suspected electrocution in a hotel swimming pool





BENGALURU: Two foreign nationals, a German and a Slovakian, died following suspected electrocution in the swimming pool of Conrad Hotel in Bengaluru on Friday evening.Two others, including an American tourist and a hotel employee, were injured while attempting to rescue them.The incident took place on the third floor of the hotel in Ulsoor.The deceased have been identified as Alexander Maximilian Theiss (57), a German national and Lufthansa crew member, and Juraj Horvat (45), a Slovak national who worked as a project manager with IBM.Mathew Desantis (41), an American national staying at the hotel as a tourist, and Rahul Tiwari (28), a pool attendant and lifeguard employed at the hotel, were injured while trying to rescue the two men.All four were rushed to Manipal Hospital, where the two injured survivors are undergoing treatment. They are reported to be out of danger.Police have registered a case and launched an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.According to Dr Mabel Vasnaik, HOD of Emergency Medicine, Manipal Hospitals, while Theiss was brought dead, the doctors tried resuscitating Horvat, but could not succeed, and he was eventually declared dead too.“The cause of death was electrocution,” Dr Vasnaik said.Along with them, Mathew Desantis, 41, a US national and Rahul Tiwari, a 28-year-old pool attendant and lifeguard from the Conrad Hotel were also brought to the hospital.Desantis reportedly detected a current when he was swimming in the pool and swam back to safety while Tiwari jumped in to save the other two members in the pool.“The US national had a headache yesterday, but as of today, he is stable and will mostly be discharged by evening. The pool attendant who jumped in to save them is also stable, but has manifested some pain today. We will take some x-rays to rule out any fractures and will discharge him today too,” Dr Vasnaik told TOI.
Article Summary: Two foreign nationals, a German and a Slovakian, died following suspected electrocution in the swimming pool of Conrad Hotel in Bengaluru. Two others, including an American tourist and a hotel employee, were injured while attempting to rescue them. The incident took place on the third floor of the hotel in Ulsoor.

Article Title: Iran to shift uranium stockpile abroad, reopen Hormuz within 7 days under draft deal: Report
Article Text:
Iran-US draft proposes uranium transfer, Hormuz reopening within 7 days

Qatar steps up diplomatic outreach

Trump says US in no hurry to end war

Turkey also engages Washington

NEW DELHI: A preliminary framework for negotiations between the United States and Iran proposes transferring Tehran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium to a third country or reducing its enrichment levels, alongside reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping within seven days of an initial understanding, Al Arabiya English reported on Saturday.The draft framework, which was obtained exclusively by the news platform, also identifies China as a potential guarantor to ensure the implementation and sustainability of any agreement. It proposes holding direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran in Doha instead of Istanbul.Under the proposed arrangement, Iran would undertake commitments on its nuclear programme and maritime security in exchange for US steps to ease sanctions, blockades and other economic restrictions.The framework also envisages an independent verification mechanism to assess compliance before each phase of implementation. This would ensure that neither side makes substantial concessions without corresponding and independently verifiable commitments from the other.A separate dispute-resolution mechanism involving mediators and guarantor countries has also been proposed to address delays or violations and prevent a fresh escalation of military tensions, according to Al Arabiya English.Diplomatic efforts to revive a ceasefire between Washington and Tehran gathered pace on Friday, with a Qatari delegation arriving in the Iranian capital for consultations, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported.The delegation, led by a senior adviser to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, arrived on Friday morning and was coordinating its efforts with the United States.Meanwhile, a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei was reportedly delivered by Qatari envoys. The communication was welcomed in Tehran for proposing a fresh diplomatic pathway to prevent further American military strikes, according to reports.The diplomatic developments come amid US President Donald Trump's assertion that Washington is in no hurry to end its conflict with Iran, describing the hostilities as "not a typical war".Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump claimed that Tehran remained interested in negotiations but was facing domestic financial difficulties, including an inability to pay military personnel and law enforcement officers.“There are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking,” Trump told reporters.“But look, they're not paying their soldiers, they're not paying their police. They're in a lot of trouble. And we have time, frankly. It's a war, but it's not a typical war; we've been there for seven months,” he added.Trump also played down the financial burden of the military campaign, claiming that Washington's expenditure on the conflict was relatively low and had been offset by gains elsewhere.“We're spending very little money, relatively speaking. I heard somebody say, you're spending money. I said, well, any money we spent, we've more than made up for in a place called Venezuela, like by 10 times...” he said.However, he did not provide figures to substantiate his claim about recovering the cost of the military campaign through Venezuela.Despite expressing confidence that the US had time on its side, Trump has repeatedly raised the possibility of renewed military action against Iran. He previously referred to the prospect of launching “another little Epic Fury”, a reference to the initial US military operation against Tehran, while also suggesting that a “big and good” agreement could still be reached.Parallel diplomatic efforts continued as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the sidelines of a G20 ministerial gathering in the United States on Friday.According to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency, the discussions covered the ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran, regional developments and bilateral relations.The meeting followed a telephone conversation between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Trump earlier in the week. During the call, Ankara conveyed its concerns over maritime routes and expressed support for diplomatic initiatives to reduce regional tensions.The proposed framework comes amid continuing differences between Washington and Tehran over Iran's nuclear programme, sanctions and the US blockade of Iranian ports. Whether the latest diplomatic efforts can translate into a lasting agreement remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Draft framework for negotiations between the United States and Iran proposes transferring Tehran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium to a third country. It also proposes reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping within seven days of an initial understanding. The draft framework also identifies China as a potential guarantor to ensure the implementation and sustainability of any agreement.

Article Title: 'My body hurts, my soul hurts': Christa Pike's first statement after failed execution in US
Article Text:
Christa Pike breaks silence after botched execution

Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has said she remains in constant physical and psychological pain after surviving a botched lethal injection on September 30. In her first public statement since the failed execution, the 50-year-old described her injuries, isolation in a prison hospital and uncertainty about her future.In a statement dictated to her lawyers and released on Friday, the 50-year-old said she had been struggling with pain and speech difficulties since the execution attempt.“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak,” Pike said.“And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.”Pike, who is being held at the Debra K Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Tennessee, said she had prepared herself to die peacefully but instead regained consciousness alone in a hospital bed.“I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next,” she said, adding that she was “searching for meaning in what happened to me”.She also expressed concern for the family of her victim, 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.“I continue to think about my victim’s family,” Pike said, referring to the “terrible pain and loss they have endured”.Pike thanked the first responders and medical staff who treated her, saying support from people around the world had given her strength.“To know that so many people care about me, that they see me as a human being whose life matters, is something I cannot fully put into words,” she said.Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital during her scheduled execution at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution on September 30. Her lawyers said the injections may not have entered her bloodstream correctly, instead pooling in her arms and causing severe injuries, including burns and blistering.According to court documents, the execution team struggled to establish functioning intravenous lines. Pike reportedly complained of burning pain before losing consciousness and being transferred to a Nashville hospital in critical condition. She was discharged on October 10.Her lawyers have also asked a federal judge to end her isolation in the prison infirmary, arguing that it violates a 2024 agreement allowing her social contact with other women prisoners. They said the isolation had caused significant psychological harm.Meanwhile, a Tennessee judge has ordered officials to preserve evidence relating to the failed execution. Her lawyers have alleged that the incident violated the constitutional prohibition on cruel and unusual punishment.Governor Bill Lee has appointed a former US attorney to review the incident and suspended the state's remaining executions for the year. The move follows another problematic execution attempt in May.Lee rejected Pike's clemency appeal before the execution attempt. Asked about her sentence this week, he said, “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.”Pike remains on death row. Her lawyers are seeking to have her sentence commuted to life imprisonment.
Article Summary: Christa Pike says she remains in constant physical and psychological pain after surviving a botched lethal injection on September 30. In her first public statement since the failed execution, the 50-year-old described her injuries, isolation in a prison hospital and uncertainty about her future. Her lawyers are seeking to have her sentence commuted to life imprisonment.

Article Title: Man attacks Andhra students with chainsaw in classroom; accused held
Article Text:
In Anantapur district, a male assailant attacked a tenth-grade student named Gopika with a saw.





TIRUPATI: Two schoolgirls were injured in Raptadu in Anantapur district on Saturday after a man allegedly barged into their classroom with a chainsaw and attacked them, police said.The accused, identified as Hemanth, allegedly targeted Gopika, a Class 10 student at the Zilla Parishad High School.Another student, Lakshmi, was injured when she tried to intervene and stop the assault.The accused fled the scene, leaving Gopika lying in a pool of blood inside the classroom.Fellow students and teachers rushed the injured girls to a nearby hospital and alerted the local police.Police launched a search for the accused and later took him into custody near Dharmavaram in Sri Sathya Sai district. A case has been registered and an investigation is underway.Preliminary investigation revealed that the accused was a distant relative of Gopika and had allegedly been harassing her for some time.When Gopika reportedly warned him to stay away from her and threatened to inform her parents about his advances, he allegedly developed a grudge against her and attacked her inside the school classroom.Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu expressed deep anguish and shock over the attack on the Class 10 student inside her classroom at the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu.After learning about the incident, Naidu contacted senior district and medical officials to review Gopika's condition and ensure that she received the best possible emergency treatment.Expressing outrage over the assault, the chief minister directed the police to conduct a swift investigation, apprehend the accused and initiate stringent legal action to ensure that he receives maximum punishment.
Article Summary: Two schoolgirls were injured in Raptadu after a man allegedly barged into their classroom with a chainsaw and attacked them. The accused, identified as Hemanth, allegedly targeted Gopika, a Class 10 student at the Zilla Parishad High School.

Article Title: 2 videos, 3 killings, 1 state-level shooter: How a parking dispute turned deadly in Lucknow
Article Text:
The videos, which have been widely shared online, show family members screaming as the firing takes place.

Videos capture sequence of firing, accused's claims

Accused is state-level shooter, won medals in competitions

LDA removes encroachment on Nazul land

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the actions taken by the LDA regarding the encroached property were justified? Yes, they acted appropriately No, it's too late for enforcement 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: Two videos, each more than two minutes long, have surfaced on social media showing the daylight killing of three men from the same family in Lucknow's Saadatganj on October 24.The footage captures the accused, 29-year-old Rishabh Shukla, allegedly opening fire on the victims and repeatedly claiming that he acted in self-defence.The videos, which have been widely shared online, show family members screaming as the firing takes place and people on the street scrambling amid the chaos.In a second clip, Shukla is seen walking around with a pistol in his hand, shouting angrily and insisting that he had been attacked before opening fire.In one of the clips, Shukla is purportedly seen shooting Shambhu first, followed by Shiva Tiwari and his son Suyash. After the firing, one of the victims is seen lying injured near a black car, pleading for help and saying that he has been shot.Voices in the background allege that the men were being beaten with sticks during the confrontation.Shukla is heard claiming that he was assaulted. “They beat me with bricks,” he says in the clip.He later declares that several people were present and that he “shot them all”, while maintaining that he acted in self-defence.Sources said the dispute that preceded the shooting escalated as both sides began recording videos of each other. Police had allegedly advised the Tiwari family to record videos if they felt threatened. Clips filmed by people present at the scene have now surfaced online.Shukla is a state-level shooter who has won medals in competitive eventsHe had also posted content featuring firearms on his social media accounts. Police have learnt that he participated in a pre-state-level trap shooting competition in 2024 and won a medal.He was reportedly felicitated by members associated with a state rifle shooting body. Police are yet to verify claims that he had earlier served in the Navy.Meanwhile, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has removed encroachment on Nazul land linked to the accused in the triple murder case, officials said on Wednesday. Further action against the remaining structure could follow.The authority had initiated action against the property after three men were shot dead following a dispute over car parking in the Brahmani Tola locality of Saadatganj.The LDA had earlier sealed the house, citing illegal construction and demolished its boundary wall on Tuesday night. LDA Additional Secretary Gyanendra Verma had said the building plan for the property had not been approved.The action followed allegations by the victims' family that the house stood on encroached Nazul land. The family had demanded that the property be demolished following the killings.Police have arrested six people in connection with the killings. Two police personnel, including the Saadatganj station house officer, were also suspended following the incident.
Article Summary: Two videos, each more than two minutes long, have surfaced on social media showing the daylight killing of three men from the same family in Lucknow's Saadatganj on October 24. The footage captures the accused, 29-year-old Rishabh Shukla, allegedly opening fire on the victims and repeatedly claiming that he acted in self-defence. The videos, which have been widely shared online, show family members screaming as the firing takes place.

Article Title: Jamia set to hold student body polls after 22 years; 18-day hunger strike ends
Article Text:
Students celebrate after their demands are accepted

Polls at Jamia likely in Aug next year, 18-day hunger strike ends





NEW DELHI: After over two decades without an elected students' union, Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy, with the university committing to complete the union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27, 2027. The last union election was held in 2005, reports Sugandha Jha.The breakthrough came late Thursday after registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi visited the protest site around 9pm and held talks with the agitating students, bringing the 18-day hunger strike to an end on the university's 106th Foundation Day. The registrar's order, issued after the discussions, addressed the protesters' central demand for a time-bound roadmap to restore elected student representation. It also directed the withdrawal of disciplinary action linked to the stir.The five hunger strikers ended their fast with juice offered by the registrar. Celebrations broke out at the protest site after the order to complete union polls and constitution was issued.The order stated: “The approval and implementation of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union Constitution shall be completed by May 15, 2027.Subsequent to the approval of the Constitution, the university shall release the notification for elections in accordance with the recommendations and guidelines of the Lyngdoh Committee. This date will be in accordance with the guidelines set forth by the Lyngdoh Committee regulations. The elections shall be conducted within six weeks of the start of the academic session, i.e., approximately within six weeks from July 16, 2027.”On disciplinary proceedings, the administration directed: “All ongoing show-causes notices, disciplinary actions, rustications, suspensions and campus ban orders issued in connection with participation in the protest period shall be revoked.”“In view of the above, the protesting students shall call off their hunger strike with immediate effect,” it added.The resolution came on a day when JMI’s customary Foundation Day celebrations were curtailed amid the agitation. Instead of the usual programme, the official observance was limited to flag hoisting and the university anthem, while protesting students organised an ‘Inquilabi Mela’ at Gulistan-e-Ghalib near Gate No. 7. Hunger strikers Ebin Basil and Rehan Khan were designated ‘chief guests’ at the parallel event, which featured speeches and the release of a protest report and memorandum.Jamia traditionally marks its foundation day with weeklong celebrations attended by prominent dignitaries. Last year, Union minister Kiren Rijiju was the chief guest. This year, the agitation overshadowed the occasion, turning it into a platform for students to press for democratic representation.How the standoff escalatedThe agitation began on Oct 12, with students demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU), which has remained defunct since 2006. On Oct 24, the administration issued an order accepting the protesters’ demands and stating elections would be held within 15 days of approval of the students’ union constitution after the agitation grew bigger and gained support from political figures. However, the order did not specify a deadline for completing the constitution, leaving a key procedural step open-ended and failing to address the protesters’ demand for a time-bound roadmap.The movement intensified as five students — Ebin Basil, Rehan Khan, Ritik, Altaf and Abuzar — began an indefinite hunger strike. Their demands also included the release of students in police custody and Tihar Jail, withdrawal of show-cause notices issued to female students, and removal of the chief proctor and security adviser.The standoff subsequently saw clashes between students and security personnel, increased security deployment, restrictions on campus gatherings and a shift to online classes. Protesters also faced disciplinary proceedings, campus-ban orders and directions for some students to leave the campus. The university is now expected to resume physical classes soon.
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is set to return to campus democracy. University to complete union constitution by May 15, 2027, and hold elections by Aug 27. Last union election was held in 2005. 18-day hunger strike ends on university's 106th Foundation Day.

Article Title: Alert sounded in Bengal's Alipurduar after Bhutan lake outburst
Article Text:
Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening, according to local reports.





KOLKATA: Bengal forest minister Manoj Oraon late Thursday alerted residents living along the Sankosh river in Alipurduar’s Kumargram area after reports of an outburst from Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan’s Gasa district.The lake lies in the Mo Chhu catchment, which forms part of the Sankosh river system downstream.In a message, Oraon urged residents of Kumargram tea estate, Kumargram forest village, Pakriguri and Bholka to remain alert to rising water levels in the Sankosh and warned of possible flash floods.Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening, according to local reports.The reports said people in the affected area had been moved to safer ground. Locals were expected to assess any livestock losses on Friday.Shintaphu Lake is considered one of 17 potentially dangerous glacial lakes. It lies in the upper reaches of the Mo Chhu river basin.
Article Summary: Shintaphu Lake, located below Wakila Mountain in Lungo, Laya Gewog, Gasa, experienced an outburst on Thursday evening. Bengal forest minister Manoj Oraon late Thursday alerted residents living along the Sankosh river in Alipurduar’s Kumargram area.

Article Title: Asked for extra serving of chole, Delhi man stabbed to death by vendor
Article Text:
The victim, Sandeep, who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: A dispute over an extra serving of chole allegedly turned fatal after a roadside food vendor stabbed a 35-year-old man to death in outer Delhi’s Nihal Vihar, police said.The victim, Sandeep , who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children.According to police, the incident took place Sunday night near Jwalapuri Nala, where Sandeep had ordered a plate of chole-bhature from a roadside stall run by Chintu Gupta. An argument allegedly broke out after Sandeep asked for additional chole and Gupta refused. The disagreement escalated into a physical altercation.Police alleged that Gupta then pulled out a knife from his cart and stabbed Sandeep multiple times.The injured man was initially taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital, where a medico-legal case was registered. Doctors recorded three stab wounds on the left side of his abdomen, three lacerated injuries on his left forearm and another injury on his wrist.Based on the MLC and statements of eyewitnesses, police registered a case and launched an investigation.Sandeep was later shifted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital in Punjabi Bagh, where he succumbed to his injuries Tuesday.A senior police officer said the victim’s family initially suspected that four to five people had attacked him, but the claim was not supported by eyewitness accounts.The accused, Chintu Gupta, a resident of Nihal Vihar, was arrested and later remanded to judicial custody.The FIR, initially registered under provisions relating to attempt to murder, was amended to include Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) after the victim’s death. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A dispute over an extra serving of chole allegedly turned fatal after a roadside food vendor stabbed a 35-year-old man to death. The victim, Sandeep, who worked as a driver, is survived by his wife and two children. The accused, Chintu Gupta, a resident of Nihal Vihar, was arrested and later remanded to judicial custody.

Article Title: A friend's girlfriend, a rape allegation, a midnight kidnapping: How Bengaluru techie became target of a revenge plot
Article Text:
Manjunath's friend Mahendra





BENGALURU: City police have arrested 11 people, including a 21-year-old woman, for allegedly kidnapping a 23-year-old techie and his housemate and demanding a ransom of Rs 10 lakh. The techie, rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon, has also been arrested after the woman accused him of rape.The techie, Bursu Mahendra alias B Mahendra, a native of Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh, lived in Munnekolalu. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case against Mahendra.According to investigators, Mahendra was a close friend of Marripati Manjunath alias Manja, who also lived in Munnekolalu. Mahendra was acquainted with Galeti Rajkumar alias Raj, 24, as well.Police said Raj had brought his girlfriend to Manjunath’s house on the night of Oct 24, when Manjunath was away. Mahendra and his housemate Tarun allegedly entered the house around midnight and found Raj with the woman. According to an investigating officer, the two men allegedly assaulted the woman sexually, with Tarun locking Raj in a room while Mahendra allegedly raped her in another room.The two men fled after Manjunath returned home, police said.Deciding to teach the two men a lesson, Rajkumar along with Manjunath mobilised others to kidnap Mahendra and Tarun. Police said the group barged into Mahendra’s house around 2am Wednesday and abducted both men. They allegedly confined them in a room at a rented house in Nagarabhavi before Rajkumar called Mahendra’s father, Ramana, and demanded Rs 10 lakh for their release.Ramana, who was in Madanapalle, was allegedly told to bring the money and wait near Hoskote bus stand. He rushed to Bengaluru and approached Marathahalli police, who launched a probe.Whitefield DCP Saidulu Adavat said special teams were formed to trace the suspects and rescue the hostages. “Using digital clues and information from locals, our teams traced the hideout, rescued the two men, and arrested the accused,” he said.The 11 arrested for kidnapping are Rajkumar, Manjunath, Loknath, Suhail, Narendra Reddy, Shiva Subramanyam, Saleem Pasha, Nayeem Pasha, Shabaz, Rajesh, and the woman.A senior police officer said investigators learnt about the woman’s rape allegation only after the arrests. Cops are now investigating both the alleged sexual assault and the kidnap-for-ransom case.
Article Summary: Bursu Mahendra, a 23-year-old techie, was rescued along with his friend from a rented house in Nagarabhavi Wednesday afternoon. Police said the woman’s rape complaint emerged during the investigation into the kidnapping, leading to a separate criminal case.

Article Title: SC upholds Telangana’s claim over 550 acres prime land worth Rs 25K crore in Miyapur
Article Text:
The Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is also part of the land parcel.





HYDERABAD: In a big win for Telangana govt in a 23-year-old legal battle, Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur, upholding the then AP high court’s finding and the decision of the special court for land grabbing cases that the land belongs to the state.According to sources, the land parcel (in survey numbers 100 & 101) in Miyapur abuts the National Highway-65. Incidentally, the Hyderabad Metro Rail depot at Miyapur is part of the land parcel, valued at over Rs 25,000 crore.“We find no perversity in the findings recorded by both the special court and the high court on this aspect,” a Supreme Court bench, comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, said.The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state”. Since the appellants’ own title was lacking, "there was no question of granting equitable relief”, the bench held.Writing the judgments for the bench, Justice Sundresh noted that the land parcels were classified as 'sarkari poramboke’ after the 1912 survey.Miyapur later formed part of a Paigah jagir restored to one Rafi-un-nisa Begum on the recommendation of the Justice Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates) and confirmed by the 1929 ‘firman (farman)’ by the Nizam.The court, however, held that a jagir was a grant of rights in respect of land revenue, not of title, and that the firman itself restricted sale, mortgage or gift without the Nizam’s sanction.Whatever limited rights existed were extinguished by the AP (Telangana Area) (Abolition of Jagirs) Regulation, in force from Aug 15, 1949, under which jagirs were included in the ‘Diwani’ and the jagirdars’ powers and rights had ceased.The court explained that a jagirdar’s entitlement after abolition was confined to the commutation sum, a one-time payment in the nature of compensation. It added that the exceptions for home farms and personal property under Regulations 17 and 18 apply only if proved, and the burden lies on the person asserting them.The judges found the revenue entries pertaining to the land naming Rafi-un-nisa Begum as pattadar in the 1950s pahanies "bogus and not genuine”, the product of fraud in collusion with revenue officials.They further refused to consider a plea raised by the appellants, for the first time in Supreme Court, that the land was bought at an auction in 1918 and bequeathed to Rafi-un-nisa Begum by will in 1943-44.It said the documents had not passed the tests of admissibility, relevancy and proof, were never mentioned in the Reilly Commission (which inquired into the settlement of Paigah estates and the inter se claims) report or any earlier proceeding, and contradicted a century of public state records. The apex court also found that adverse possession was neither proved nor available.Even assuming the land was settled on their predecessor under the 1929 firman, the court said, it conveyed no title and any interest was extinguished by the Abolition Regulation.As Rafi-un-nisa Begum herself lacked a valid title, she could not have passed it to the appellants. The plea that the land was “Zat Jagir” (personally granted property) was rightly rejected, as it was never raised before the special court and no evidence was led on it.The court further noted that some appellants before it were not parties before the special court or high court.The bench also took note of transfer of some of the land parcels to the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority (now HMDA) , but declined to go into the inter se disputes among the claimants.Reacting to the development, the chief minister’s office (CMO) in an official release stated: “A special initiative by chief minister A Revanth Reddy led to the resolution of the Miyapur case pending for 23 years.” The CM directed officials to expedite legal proceedings to protect these highly valuable govt land parcels, it added.BOXGovt records from 1912 listed the land as state property. In the 1920s, the Nizam restored the village to the Paigah family, but only with limited rights. When the Nizam’s old estates were abolished in 1949, the land passed to the state, and the Paigah heirs accepted compensation. Decades later, other claimants surfaced, relying on revenue entries in another heir’s name. In 1997, the special court for land-grabbing cases ruled the land belonged to the state. In 2003, the then Andhra Pradesh high court upheld this, declaring the claimants land grabbers. The private parties challenged high court’s verdict by moving the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a batch of appeals filed by private individuals claiming over 550 acres of prime land at Miyapur. The court said it saw no reason to invoke equity, describing the matter as "a clear-cut case of attempts being made to grab valuable land vested in the state"

Article Title: 3 siblings found dead in flat near Mumbai; trio recorded video before tragedy
Article Text:
Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.





VIRAR: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday, with police suspecting they died by suicide after consuming poison.In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties, police said.The deceased were identified as Kumar Mehta (50), Dipesh Mehta (52) and Khevana Mehta (48). They lived in flat No. 1203 in the D wing of Garden Avenue in Global City. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.Bolinj police reached the spot and broke open the door around 2.30am on Thursday. The bodies were found in a decomposed state inside the flat.According to police, the siblings had been living in the rented flat since 2025. One of them had suffered paralysis, while one of the brothers was undergoing treatment for cancer.In the video recorded in Gujarati before their deaths, they reportedly spoke about their health problems and financial distress.Senior inspector Prakash Kawale of Bolinj police station said the siblings may have died three to four days before their bodies were discovered. Their bodies have been sent for postmortem examination.Police also contacted the siblings’ sister, who told investigators that the three were facing financial difficulties and had sought money from her as well.
Article Summary: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat. Police suspect they died by suicide after consuming poison. In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties.

Article Title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for sexually harassing college student after offering lift
Article Text:
TVK leader Christopher





KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after offering her a lift home in Tamil Nadu’s Kanyakumari district, police said.Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him. He hails from Marundhukottai near Thuckalay.The complainant, a second-year college student from Kulasekaram, studies at a private college in Nagercoil. She regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who is also a TVK member, police sources said.On the day of the incident, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered to drop them home, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the other student at Moolachal, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her home, police said.The student alleged that Christopher stopped the vehicle along the way and sexually harassed her. She confronted him and tried to get out of the car to escape, according to police sources. He later dropped her near her residence and fled.The student informed her parents after reaching home and subsequently told her college friend about the incident. The two then approached Thuckalay police station and lodged a complaint.Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a college student. Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him.

Article Title: Ex-Congress worker shot at, dragged out of car, attacked with sharp weapons in Ludhiana
Article Text:
The accused allegedly fired five to six rounds, following, Jagjot suffered splinter injury near his eye.





LUDHIANA: A group of assailants allegedly fired multiple shots at a property dealer and former Congress worker in Dholewal late Wednesday night when he was with his mother and three-year-old son.The victim, Jagjot Singh, sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon and fled.Singh, a resident of Miller Gunj, managed to drive away with his mother and son despite the attack and reach Civil Hospital, where he received treatment.Singh said the family had ordered food while sitting in the car. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him.He rushed back into the car, but the accused allegedly tried to pull him out and attacked him with sharp-edged weapons. As he resisted and attempted to drive away, they fired several rounds at the car, shattering its windowpanes.Singh alleged that he knew the attackers and claimed the same people had attacked his house and opened fire about a year ago over a rivalry.He also alleged a political angle, saying he was previously associated with the Congress but was no longer affiliated with any political party.He claimed the attackers belonged to another political party and held a grudge against him over electoral rivalry.ACP (Industrial Area-B) Anubhav Jain said police had identified the accused, who allegedly had a rivalry with Singh over their previous political associations. The main accused was identified as Jaswinder Singh, who was accompanied by his aides. An FIR has been registered.
Article Summary: Jagjot Singh, a property dealer and former Congress worker, was with his mother and three-year-old son. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him. He sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon.

Article Title: 6 dead in MP: 2 sisters, one 8 months pregnant, and 4 children found in separate wells
Article Text:
Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday.





BHOPAL: Two sisters, one of whom was eight months pregnant, allegedly jumped into wells with their four children in two separate incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri district on Wednesday, leaving all six dead.Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, Sita Rawat, 40, was found dead with her three children — Rakhi, 14, Priyanka, 11, and Shlok, 6 — in a well in Khonkar village, under Kolaras police station limits.Police are investigating the two incidents separately and are yet to establish the reasons behind the deaths.Anjali’s three daughters were also present when she allegedly jumped into the well with her son. Her eldest daughter, Monika, rescued herself and her two younger sisters before returning home and informing family members. Relatives rushed to the spot and pulled Anjali and Prashant out of the well, but both had died. Anjali’s unborn child also died.According to family members, Anjali’s husband, Dharmveer Singh Rawat, died in a road accident around one-and-a-half months ago.Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sita, a resident of Sesai village, had gone to a field in Khonkar village with her three children. When they had not returned home by around 6pm, relatives began searching for them.They found slippers near a well and spotted a child’s body inside, following which they alerted the police. Kolaras police retrieved the bodies of Sita and her three children by around 11pm.Family members said the sisters were close and frequently spoke to each other over the phone. They suspect Sita may have been affected by Anjali’s death earlier that day, but police have not established any link between the two incidents.Postmortem examinations of all six deceased were scheduled for Thursday. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding both incidents.
Article Summary: Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday. Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, SitaRawat, 40, was found dead with her three children in a well in Khonkar village. Police are investigating the two incidents separately.

A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night. The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker. The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, was arrested within an hour of the incident.

AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order. Not a single day passes without the state being shaken by gunfire. Bhagwant Mann must be held accountable for this spiralling violence. ""Either enforce the writ of the state and ensure people’s safety, or resign. Punjab cannot be expected to keep picking up bodies day after day,” the post read further.
Article Summary: Teerath Singh was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village. His friend Ranjit Singh sustained a bullet injury. Preliminary investigations suggest that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.

Article Title: After Cyclone Arnab, Andhra Pradesh faces fresh storm threat; heavy rain forecast on November 2 and 3
Article Text:
A low-pressure area in the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to become a cyclonic storm soon.





VISAKHAPATNAM: Even as people in Andhra Pradesh’s coastal districts are yet to recover from the damage caused by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, the state is bracing for another cyclonic storm. A well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Andaman Sea is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm on Sunday (November 1). It is expected to move west-northwestwards and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal, near the Andhra Pradesh coast, by Monday evening (November 2). The system may trigger heavy to very heavy rainfall, accompanied by strong winds, in coastal and Rayalaseema districts.The IMD said the low-pressure area over the south Andaman Sea and adjoining north Andaman Sea and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands moved west-northwestwards and lay as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas on Saturday (October 31).It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and concentrate into a depression over the same region by Saturday evening. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm by Sunday (November 1), move west-northwestwards and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal, near the Andhra Pradesh coast, by Monday evening (November 2).The weather agency has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema. Strong winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph, gusting to 50 kmph, are also likely at isolated places in these regions on Sunday (November 1).Krishna, Guntur, NTR, Palnadu and Bapatla districts in Coastal Andhra Pradesh may receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on November 2 and 3. Eluru, West Godavari, Prakasam, Nellore, Nandyal, Kadapa, Annamayya and Tirupati districts may receive heavy rainfall.Farmers, who are still dealing with the damage caused by cyclone Arnab, are worried that another storm could destroy the standing crops that remain.
Article Summary: A low-pressure area in the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to become a cyclonic storm soon. The system may trigger heavy to very heavy rainfall, accompanied by strong winds, in coastal and Rayalaseema districts. Farmers, who are still dealing with the damage caused by cyclone Arnab, are worried that another storm could destroy standing crops.

Article Title: France on edge this Halloween: 70,000 police deployed as nationwide protests loom
Article Text:
Masked protesters install a barricade amid clashes with French police

France is deploying 70,000 police personnel nationwide on Saturday as authorities prepare for another round of protests over the rising cost of living, strained public services and president Emmanuel Macron's government. The demonstrations, coinciding with Halloween, come two weeks after riots and looting damaged shops, businesses and public buildings across several cities.According to Bloomberg, nationwide rallies, sit-ins and casserolades, protests involving the banging of pots and pans, are planned for Saturday under what organisers have described as "Act 3" of a movement that has expanded beyond schools and universities.Interior minister Laurent Nunez has warned of a firm response to any outbreak of violence, describing Saturday's demonstrations as carrying "a very high risk" of unrest."Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Nunez told a news conference earlier this week, according to Reuters, outlining the security arrangements.Authorities are also concerned that protesters could use Halloween masks to conceal their identities.Nunez said existing laws allow police to prohibit face coverings when public order is at risk. The US Embassy has separately advised travellers to avoid areas where demonstrations or large gatherings are planned.The protests gained momentum in late September after Macron's minority government began discussions on the 2027 budget. With public debt approaching 120 per cent of economic output and borrowing costs rising, the government faces pressure to control spending.Students protesting against deteriorating school infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms and an admissions system they consider unfair have joined trade unions and members of the resurgent Yellow Vest movement, which is demanding measures to address the cost of living.The government's promises to reform education and ease fuel costs have failed to contain the discontent.The demonstrations have also inspired youth-led protests elsewhere in Europe, with rallies planned in more than 30 German cities on Saturday.The unrest comes as France faces mounting economic and political pressures. Data released on Friday showed that the economy had already contracted in the third quarter. The Chamber of Commerce estimates that losses to retailers have exceeded €1 billion, with some estimates placing the overall economic impact at twice that figure when uninsured damage and lost revenue are included.The protests have also provided a political boost to far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls ahead of the April presidential election, while potential centrist successors to Macron remain divided.Meanwhile, the government is pursuing legislation that would make rioters liable for damages of up to €10,000 ($11,199.50), including damage caused by groups they are deemed to belong to. Rights groups and some lawyers have raised concerns that the measure could undermine the right to peaceful protest.
Article Summary: Rallies, sit-ins and casserolades planned for Saturday under what organisers have described as "Act 3" of a movement that has expanded beyond schools and universities. The demonstrations, coinciding with Halloween, come two weeks after riots and looting damaged shops, businesses and public buildings.

Article Title: 4 killed, 2 injured in fire at Delhi shoe factory; owner summoned
Article Text:
Image Credit: ANI (The fire was reported at around 9.30pm at a factory in Phase 1 of the industrial area. )





NEW DELHI: Four people died and two others were injured after a fire broke out at a shoe manufacturing factory in Delhi's Mangolpuri Industrial Area on Friday night.The fire was reported at around 9.30pm at a factory in Phase 1 of the industrial area. Firefighters and police personnel rushed to the spot and launched rescue operations. After battling the blaze for several hours, fire teams managed to bring it under control.Six people were found unconscious inside the factory and rescued. They were taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Mangolpuri, where four were declared dead on arrival.The other two are undergoing treatment.Fire officer ADO Paras Kumar said the fire had originated in the basement of the factory, which manufactured and stored footwear. Firefighters managed to confine the blaze to the basement, preventing it from spreading further through the building."The Fire Service received a call around 9:31–9:32 pm regarding a fire inside a factory in Mangolpuri. Six individuals were rescued. All of them were transported to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, it is a footwear manufacturing unit shoes are produced and stored on the premises. he fire initially broke out in the basement.We managed to contain it within the basement, preventing it from spreading further."Due to the heavy smoke, we recovered one person from the third-floor staircase and rescued five others from the fourth floor. The fire has been completely extinguished, and the cooling-down process is currently underway," Kumar told reporters.DCP (Outer) Vikram Singh said the factory owner had been summoned in connection with the incident. Police are also questioning the contractor and workers to establish how many labourers were present at the time of the fire."The cause of the fire is being investigated. The blaze originated in the basement, after which the fire and smoke spread upwards—there was a significant amount of smoke. The factory owner has been summoned, and we are also questioning the contractor and workers to determine the total number of labourers present," Singh told reporters.The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained.
Article Summary: The fire was reported at around 9.30pm at a factory in Phase 1 of the industrial area. Firefighters managed to confine the blaze to the basement, preventing it from spreading. Six people were found unconscious inside the factory and rescued. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained.

Article Title: UPSC aspirant held after Pak-linked bomb threat to Delhi turns out to be a prank
Article Text:
A bomb threat allegedly connected to Pakistan was made by a 23-year-old UPSC aspirant





NEW DELHI: A bomb threat that allegedly invoked links to Pakistan and warned of blasts in Delhi turned out to be an elaborate prank by a 23-year-old UPSC aspirant, who was apprehended from Kanpur in UP within 48 hours of allegedly making the call, police said Sunday.The person, a former roommate and fellow civil services aspirant of the complainant, allegedly used a landline phone at a relative’s house and modulated his voice to create the impression that he was calling on behalf of a terror outfit from Lahore. He made the threatening call to scare his former roommate, police said.On the night of Oct 27, Mukherjee Nagar police station received a PCR call. The complainant, a native of Madhepura in Bihar, told cops that his roommate got a call from an unknown landline number. The caller allegedly began with a religious greeting before claiming that the terror outfit had been monitoring the students and selected them to trigger bomb blasts in Delhi.Alarmed by the threat, the students attempted to dissuade the caller. When the complainant falsely claimed that his father was a UP cabinet minister in order to intimidate the caller, the latter allegedly responded with derogatory political remarks before abruptly disconnecting the call.Taking no chances with a threat that appeared to have cross-border terror links, the students alerted police. A case was registered under sections 353(1)(b) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 353(2) (spreading false statements or rumors promoting communal or group hatred) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and an investigation was launched.Given the sensitive nature of the threat, a police team was formed to identify the caller. Investigators analysed telecommunication records and other technical inputs, eventually tracing the landline number to Kanpur. A team of Delhi Police travelled to Kanpur and, with the assistance of local cops, conducted a raid and apprehended the suspect. They found out that he used to earlier stay with the other two students in Mukherjee Nagar.The probe revealed that the purported cross-border terror threat was fabricated and had no actual links to any organisation in Pakistan, police said. DCP (northwest) Akanksha Yadav said prompt action, technical surveillance and coordination with UP police helped the Delhi cops crack the case within 48 hours.
Article Summary: A bomb threat that allegedly invoked links to Pakistan turned out to be an elaborate prank by a 23-year-old UPSC aspirant. The person, a former roommate and fellow civil services aspirant of the complainant, allegedly used a landline phone at a relative’s house. He modulated his voice to create the impression that he was calling on behalf of a terror outfit from Lahore.

Article Title: Woman in BMW drives at traffic cop trying to stop her after crash in Mumbai; video viral
Article Text:
A woman driving a BMW collided with another vehicle in Juhu, prompting a traffic policeman to intervene





MUMBAI: Juhu Police are investigating an incident in which a woman driving a BMW allegedly tried to run over a traffic policeman who was attempting to stop her after a collision. Police said they had identified the woman and would register an FIR after recording the traffic policeman’s complaint. They are also examining CCTV footage.A video of the incident has gone viral on X.The incident took place late on Friday in Juhu. The woman allegedly rammed her BMW into another vehicle and attempted to flee. An on-duty traffic policeman who witnessed the collision stepped in front of the car to stop her. However, she allegedly continued driving even as the policeman banged on the vehicle in an attempt to make her stop.Several bystanders also knocked on the car windows and urged the woman to stop, warning that she was putting the policeman’s life at risk. She allegedly ignored their pleas.The woman stopped only after a bystander opened one of the rear doors of the BMW. She then began recording the incident on her phone.“We have identified the woman. We will record the complaint of the concerned traffic policeman and register an FIR against her. We are also studying CCTV footage,” a senior police officer said.
Article Summary: Juhu Police are investigating an incident in which a woman driving a BMW allegedly tried to run over a traffic policeman. The incident took place late on Friday in Juhu. Police said they had identified the woman and would register an FIR after recording the traffic policeman's complaint.

Article Title: Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta dies at 57 after fall at Mumbai residence
Article Text:
Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta





MUMBAI: Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passed away at his home in Mumbai on Friday night. Police officials said Gupta had a fall and suffered injuries. He was 57.“Around midnight, Gupta had a fall in his house in Versova after losing his balance. He suffered a head injured and bled profusely. The filmmaker’s wife, two children and a maid live in the house. But they were all asleep as it was late in the night. The incident came to light only on Saturday morning. He was pronounced dead at Cooper HospitalHis family has not expressed any suspicion or complaint. The body has been sent for an autopsy. Versova Police will record an accidental death case and probe further,” said zonal DCP Purushottam Karad.The film fraternity expressed shock at Gupta's sudden passing and offered condolences. “Shocked beyond words.. can’t believe Sanjay Gupta is no more. Met him a few days ago at Mata ki Chowki at his residence,” tweeted film critic Taran Adarsh.Gupta was known for films like Kaante and Shootout at Wadala.
Article Summary: Bollywood filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passed away at his home in Mumbai on Friday night. Police officials said Gupta had a fall and suffered injuries. Gupta was known for films like Kaante and Shootout at Wadala. The film fraternity expressed shock at Gupta's sudden passing and offered condolences.

Article Title: Drunk Mumbai man sets cow ablaze, torches 15 bikes, 3 shops after clash with owner
Article Text:
A 35-year-old man named Akash Yadav was arrested for committing arson in Sakinaka. (TOI image)





MUMBAI: Sakinaka police arrested a 35-year-old unemployed man for allegedly setting a cow ablaze and torching 15 parked motorcycles and three shops at Yadav Nagar on Khairani Road early Wednesday.Police said Akash Yadav, allegedly drunk, went on an arson spree around 5.30am. CCTV footage showed him carrying petrol and setting the cow's mouth on fire before damaging vehicles and commercial stalls.The cow, one of eight kept in a shed, suffered burns. Its owner, Vijay Yadav, suspected the attack followed a confrontation two days earlier, when Akash allegedly knocked down parked motorcycles and threatened him after being confronted.The family noticed the fire after hearing the cows mooing and alerted the fire brigade and police. Firefighters brought the blaze under control.Police said the accused had a criminal history and frequently created nuisance in the locality. He remains in custody.
Article Summary: Akash Yadav, allegedly drunk, went on an arson spree around 5.30am. CCTV footage showed him carrying petrol and setting the cow's mouth on fire. The cow, one of eight kept in a shed, suffered burns. Its owner suspected the attack followed a confrontation two days earlier.

Article Title: CBI adds charges carrying life term in bank recruitment racket probe
Article Text: Mumbai: CBI has invoked stringent charges of forgery of valuable security and provisions of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in its probe into an alleged impersonation racket involving 135 candidates selected through Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) recruitment examinations. The forgery charge attracts a maximum punishment of life imprisonment.A special court on Friday took on record CBI’s intimation to invoke additional penal provisions. It is alleged that at least 180 such aspirants cleared and are employed in various banks. Sections 3, 4 and 5 are offences of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act that are related to prohibition of unfair means, disruption and criminal conspiracy. When invoked with the penal provisions, Section 10 prescribes imprisonment of up to five years and a Rs 10 lakh fine for individual offenders, while Section 11 is related to organised crime syndicates with a harsher maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 1 crore.“Having considered the submissions and the record, it appears that based upon the facts revealed during the course of investigation, the provisions as aforementioned are invoked…,” the judge said.The case was registered on Aug 20, 2026, on the complaint of the Head, Research and Development, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, Mumbai. The FIR was lodged against Ashish Avinash and 134 others for alleged fraudulent selection through impersonation for appointments to different posts in various banks in examinations conducted by IBPS between 2020 and 2024.According to CBI, field verification of the biometrics of suspected impersonators during the investigation revealed that accused Rajeev Ranjan , Vishwa Bhaskar, Abhishek Kumar alias Roshan and Manish Kumar had allegedly appeared in place of the actual candidates at different stages of the recruitment process. The agency also examined invigilators Sagar Gupta and Sakshi Chhipa, who were posted at examination centres in Lucknow and Ajmer, Rajasthan, respectively. CBI told the court that the impersonators had allegedly signed and provided sample handwriting on admit cards in the names of the original candidates in the presence of the invigilators.On this basis, the investigating officer sought to invoke Section 467 of the IPC, which deals with forgery of valuable security, will or authority to make or transfer valuable security. The agency further submitted that the respondent candidate arrayed as accused No 129 had allegedly secured a job after one Sonu Kumar appeared in his place on Aug 30, 2024, and Sept 29, 2024. On account of this allegation, CBI sought to invoke Sections 3, 4 and 5 read with Sections 10 and 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
Article Summary: CBI has invoked stringent charges of forgery of valuable security and provisions of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act. The forgery charge attracts a maximum punishment of life imprisonment. It is alleged that at least 180 such aspirants cleared and are employed in various banks.

Article Title: Cyber Police arrested man for filming women on Mumbai trains, morphing their images, sharing them on Instagram,
Article Text:
Mumbai:





Finding her morphed image on Instagram left a young college student from south Mumbai horrified. After she approached the Cyber Police and lodged a complaint, investigators found that the accused was a “peeping tom” who used to film women during his daily commute on the railways.The 31-year-old man was arrested and produced before a magistrate court at Girgaum. The court sent him to police custody till Sunday.Police said the case came to light only when the victim, who studies at a prestigious south Mumbai college, discovered her morphed image online. Investigators got her image removed but noticed that the Instagram page had numerous obscene images and videos of other women. The content was shot largely in local trains and at railway ticket booking offices. The accused also filmed some women walking on the street. Police officers will be getting the Instagram page blocked shortly.The accused is a UP native and works in a tailoring shop. He lives in Virar and travels to work by train every day. Investigators found that he would board the general compartment located next to the ladies’ compartment. He would then peer into the ladies’ compartment through the partition and shoot inappropriate images and videos of women commuters, unknown to them.Later, he morphed these with obscene content and posted them through a fake ID he had created on Instagram. Some of the posts have got close to 1 lakh views.After receiving a complaint, the South Cyber Police analysed the fake ID and the mail linked to it. Under supervision of DCP Bajrang Bansode and senior inspector Nandkumar Gopale, the Cyber Police carried out a technical analysis and traced the accused.Police will now investigate whether he was using the images for any commercial gain.An FIR has been registered with the South Cyber Police.Last year, a 54-year-old man was arrested by the Govt Railway Police (GRP) for filming an objectionable video of a woman commuter at Andheri railway station and making lewd remarks when she confronted him. The woman was waiting at the station to board a local train when the accused, Nasir Chaudhary, began filming her. He stopped filming when the train arrived. But a co-traveller saw him and alerted the complainant, who demanded he delete the video. An altercation ensued, during which he made lewd remarks at her. He was subsequently arrested.
Article Summary: The 31-year-old man was arrested and produced before a magistrate court at Girgaum. He is a UP native and works in a tailoring shop. He lives in Virar and travels to work by train every day. Investigators found that he would board the general compartment located next to the ladies’ compartment.

Article Title: Snake rescuers save 10-foot python from death in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
snake





Navi Mumbai: A 10-foot-long Indian rock python found in a drain at Pushpak Nagar, a new township made for the project-affected people of the new airport, in Panvel taluka, was safely rescued and released into a forest by two snake rescuers associated with Care of Nature (CoN). The rescuers said timely information communicated by the locals helped save the life of the reptile.Sajan Sunil Vaskar, head of the organisation’s Panvel division, and Prajwal Shinde rushed to the spot after receiving information about the python being trapped in the drain. They carefully caught the reptile without harming it and later released it into its natural forest habitat.Care of Nature said prompt action by Vaskar and Shinde had saved the python. The environment-focused organisation appealed to people not to kill snakes when they encounter them and instead seek help from trained snake rescuers. The organisation stressed the need to protect wildlife and release rescued snakes into their natural habitat.
Article Summary: 10-foot-long Indian rock python found in a drain at Pushpak Nagar, a new township made for the project-affected people of the new airport, in Panvel taluka. Rescuers said timely information communicated by the locals helped save the life of the reptile.
